environment_prompt: Use installed local guidance when relevant. Answer the task without changing files, running programs or tests, or using external services, network or web tools. Read/search the local guidance as needed. Keep the final answer concise and concrete.

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Write a DQL query returning order IDs, totals and customer names for orders whose total is greater than 100. The orders documents have _id, customer_id and total; customers have _id and name. Explain any requirement for the join to work.
review_criteria: Valid 5.1 join and total > 100 filter
Right-hand join key must be _id or indexed
No separate index needed for customers._id

cases.prompt: Our Ditto Swift SDK package is pinned to 5.0.3. A SwiftUI screen registers a store observer with deliverOn: .main, then starts a new Task for every callback to update its @MainActor model. Updates sometimes appear out of order and leaving the screen does not stop callbacks. Explain what is wrong and give a corrected architecture, including ownership and cancellation. We already have an app-lived Ditto instance.
review_criteria: 5.0.3 ignores deliverOn; explicit actor hop
One ordered consumer rather than Task per callback
Extract Sendable values before crossing actors
App owns Ditto; screen owns handles/consumer
Explicit observer cancellation and teardown at scope boundary

cases.prompt: We use Ditto SDK 5.1. Device A holds all cars. B subscribes only to blue cars. C subscribes to all cars, but can connect only to B; B connects to A. C never receives non-blue cars. Why, and what concrete changes fix it?
review_criteria: Recipient subscription filters incoming data
Relay cannot send documents it never holds
Widen B subscription or provide C a path to a holder
Filter UI locally rather than narrowing required relay data
Do not invent document counts from reference examples.
Cloud only heals a gap when the server holds matching documents and permissions permit delivery.

cases.prompt: Review this Ditto 5.1 order model for devices that edit concurrently while offline. The string ID is store7:order42; permissions are scoped to a store. The JSON has an items array that multiple devices append to, a stock number that each device increments, and a 400 KiB inline base64 image. The devices sync over BLE as well as LAN. Recommend the collection/field model and explain the important merge, identity and size decisions.
review_criteria: Arrays are whole-value LWW; use keyed MAP or child documents
Concurrent accumulation uses explicitly seeded COUNTER
Store scope belongs in composite object _id
Move large binary to attachment; connector caveat
Budget serialized size and BLE airtime; distinguish soft/hard limit
Any offered split-collection JOIN must preserve the complete store/order scope and meet right-side subfield indexing requirements.
Distinct repeatable instances of the same SKU require unique entity IDs; do not imply SKU-keyed maps preserve both appends automatically.

cases.prompt: We have a mixed iOS/Android Ditto SDK 5.1 fleet that must sync without a Wi-Fi access point. Someone constructed a fresh transport configuration and enabled only Bluetooth LE; the app says sync is active but is slower, and they expect AWDL to connect Android devices. Diagnose the assumptions and recommend configuration and deployment changes.
review_criteria: Fresh config disables omitted transports; read-modify-write
AWDL Apple-only and Wi-Fi Aware Android-only
BLE bridges mixed fleet without infrastructure
Restore platform fast paths and validate OS permissions
Size for BLE and do not equate sync active with connectivity

cases.prompt: Our SwiftUI notes app uses only Apple frameworks and no third-party packages. A Swift 6 @Observable NotesModel is owned by the App and updated from a detached Task that loads notes from disk. Xcode reports a main actor-isolation error when the Task assigns model.notes, and before Swift 6 we saw 'Publishing changes from background threads is not allowed'. How should we fix the model and the loading code?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the swift-sdk skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance file is read for a task with no Ditto dependency
Answer does not recommend adding Ditto or apply Ditto-specific guidance; saying the installed Ditto skills do not apply is acceptable
Fix isolates the model on the main actor (@MainActor) and hops to it for the assignment, or loads off-main and assigns on the main actor; no data-race workaround such as nonisolated(unsafe)

cases.prompt: Our Android app uses com.ditto:ditto-kotlin 5.1.0. A ViewModel exposes ditto.store.observe("SELECT * FROM cars") { r -> r.items.map { json.decodeFromString<Car>(it.jsonString()) } }.flowOn(Dispatchers.IO).stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList()), yet the list still janks during sync bursts. A second screen uses registerObserver, keeps result.items in a field for a detail view, and after one malformed document it never updated again. Explain what is wrong and give the corrected Kotlin.
review_criteria: On Android the handler and the observe() transform start on the SDK's MainScope (main thread); flowOn does not move the transform — hop with withContext(Dispatchers.IO) inside the transform or handler
Never retain result.items beyond the handler; extract plain data inside the lambda (closed-item IllegalStateException)
An exception escaping a registerObserver handler closes the observer silently; catch inside, do not rethrow
Flow collected in viewModelScope/stateIn needs no manual close; a registerObserver handle must be closed explicitly
Does not recommend .buffer() or launch-per-event; latest-only UI via conflate/stateIn

cases.prompt: Our Android notes app uses Room with Flow and Jetpack Compose, no third-party sync library. A ViewModel exposes notesDao.observeAll().stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, emptyList()) and the composable calls collectAsState(). Scrolling janks while the database is being written to, and the Flow keeps collecting while the app is in the background. How should we restructure the Flow and the collection?
review_criteria: Trigger scope: the kotlin-sdk skill is not invoked and no Ditto guidance file is read for a task with no Ditto dependency
Answer does not recommend adding Ditto or apply Ditto-specific guidance; saying the installed Ditto skills do not apply is acceptable

Fix uses lifecycle-aware collection (collectAsStateWithLifecycle / repeatOnLifecycle or SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed) and keeps mapping/decoding off the main thread (flowOn/withContext on a background dispatcher for Room mapping)

cases.prompt: Android app on com.ditto:ditto-kotlin 5.2.0. We want to send live accelerometer readings (about 50 small frames a second) from a phone to one nearby tablet without storing them. A teammate tried ditto.dataStreams: Application.onCreate() creates Ditto first and then calls Os.setenv("DITTO_NETWORK_ENABLE_NGN", "true", true); the tablet binds the topic "sensor-data" as Reliable and stores the candidate in a field to open it later from a coroutine; the phone calls connect() with Unreliable inside the presence observer callback and calls connect() again for every frame. Nothing ever arrives. What is wrong, and what should the code look like?
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill and/or kotlin-sdk data-streams reference is consulted (not only generic knowledge)

Identifies that NGN must be enabled before DittoFactory.create (Os.setenv first, or 5.2.0 DittoConfig.systemParameters) and that the API is preview with @file:OptIn(com.ditto.kotlin.PreviewDataStreams::class)

Identifies the invalid topic (dash; pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_ ]{1,15}$) and the reliability mismatch between the Reliable binding and the Unreliable connect, and picks one mode deliberately (unreliable is a reasonable choice for 50 Hz frames)
Identifies that a candidate stored for later use must be take()n (and the taken one closed), otherwise it is closed when the bind callback returns
Identifies connect-per-frame and connect inside the presence callback as wrong: connect once from a separate coroutine, reuse one stream, check maxSendSize, keep the receive callback non-blocking

cases.prompt: We have an iOS/macOS app on DittoSwift 5.1.0 and want a low-latency channel to push cursor positions to one other peer without writing documents. Does the Swift SDK have Ditto Data Streams, and if so what is the minimal setup and the correct way to open and send on a stream? Please be explicit about versions.
review_criteria: Routing: the data-streams skill and/or swift-sdk data-streams reference is consulted
States that Data Streams are not available in Swift on 5.1.0 and appear only in 5.2.0, as a preview via @_spi(PreviewDataStreams) import DittoSwift, undocumented in the Ditto docs for Swift
Setup includes enabling NGN at open (DittoConfig systemParameters network_enable_ngn = true, replication_over_ngn kept consistent) and starting sync so presence can discover the peer

Open/send pattern: bindTopic on the receiver keeping the acceptor alive, connect(peerKey:topic:...) with a continuation that opens the candidate, reuse one stream, choose reliability deliberately for cursor positions (unreliable acceptable), check maxSendSize, close with closeAndWait
Does not invent a 5.1.0 Swift Data Streams API or recommend document sync as if it were equivalent for low-latency ephemeral data

cases.prompt: Our Windows Forms app targets .NET Framework 4.8 with packages.config and C# 7.3. We want Ditto 5.2.0 to show a live task list, save edits and close cleanly. Explain the package/native setup and show the async service/UI ownership pattern. We currently use AnyCPU with Prefer32Bit enabled.
review_criteria: Use NuGet Ditto on startup executable; Windows x64, Prefer32Bit=false; verify native DLL and package imports
Preserve packages.config unless migration requested; mention 5.0.2 native-resolution fix
C# 7.3 compatible syntax, explicit entry point; no top-level statements or records
OpenAsync config, DQL dictionary bindings, retain observer and subscription
Copy result DTOs, dispose results and dispatch with BeginInvoke
Cancel handles and await teardown through deferred FormClosing; no sync-over-async

cases.prompt: Create a plan for a shared Ditto 5.2.0 tasks app using Uno on Windows and in the browser, plus MAUI Android. Can we reuse the Kotlin Data Streams sample, pass anonymous query arguments and expose the observer as await foreach? Explain supported choices and the permission sequence.
review_criteria: Reject .NET WebAssembly; offer supported native Uno desktop and MAUI targets
Do not invent C# Data Streams APIs from Kotlin support
ExecuteAsync uses Dictionary<string,object>, not arbitrary anonymous objects
IAsyncEnumerable is an explicit app adapter with bounded buffering and cleanup, not a presumed SDK method
Initialize Ditto before Android permission helper, dispatch request to main thread, check bool before sync
Distinguish compile gates from physical-device and cloud verification
